utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case number IT-04-84-R77.1-T, the Prosecutor versus Shefqet Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I have the appearances? Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm Tom Hannis, aim appearing with Alma Imamovic-Ivanov. Ms. Korner is participating in an extended sitting in the Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin trial and I'm standing in for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you also for that explanation, Mr. Hannis. For the Defence, I see that you are present, Mr. Kabashi. There is an audio link established with your counsel, and I would like to verify whether Mr Karnavas is at the other side of the audio link and whether he can hear me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, I am on the other side and I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Karnavas. We will then proceed. Mr Karnavas, we already expressed that you would be excused for not being present; that has not changed. I now will proceed, first of all, with a Rule 15 bis statement. Judge Morrison is absent for urgent personal reasons this afternoon, and Judge Kwon and I have considered that it is in the interests of justice to continue to proceed despite the absence of judge Morrison, pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the rules. There seems to be some noise on the line. If it does not get any worse, then we can continue. If it does get worse, I would like a technician to have a look at it. We are sitting today to deliver the Chamber's sentencing judgement in the case of the Prosecutor versus Shefqet Kabashi. For the purposes of this hearing, I will briefly summarise the Chamber's findings. I stress that it is a summary only. The authoritative account of the Trial Chamber's findings can be found in the written sentencing judgement which will be made available at the end of this session. This case concerns Mr. Kabashi's contumacious refusal or failure to answer questions as a witness in the Haradinaj et al trial, thereby committing contempt of the Tribunal pursuant to Rule 77(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. On 26 August 2011, Mr. Kabashi pleaded guilty to two counts of contempt of the Tribunal, and the Trial Chamber accepted his plea on 31 August, entering a finding of guilt. The Trial Chamber will now give a summary of its sentencing findings. It recalled that the two primary purposes of sentencing in the Tribunal are retribution and deterrence, both special and general. The Trial Chamber considered the gravity of the offences and the totality of the culpable conduct. By contumaciously refusing or failing to answer questions as a witness, Mr. Kabashi deprived the Haradinaj et al Trial Chamber of evidence relevant for an effective ascertainment of truth in the adjudication of that case. The Defence submitted that Mr. Kabashi's frustrations, his war experience and witness intimidation may have contributed to the refusal or failure to answer questions. Despite these submissions, the Trial Chamber found that any additional motives Mr. Kabashi may have had remained vague and could not be considered in determining the appropriate sentence. In mitigation, the Trial Chamber considered that according to medical documentation, Mr. Kabashi suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder and that his medical condition worsens in a prison environment. The Trial Chamber further considered Mr. Kabashi's family situation in mitigation. Moreover, Mr. Kabashi apologised for his crime on 31 August 2011. While the Trial Chamber considered his apology genuine, it considered that the remorse expressed in this way was reduced in its mitigating weight by the fact that Mr. Kabashi had failed to come to The Hague to face the charges against him for more than four years. Having summarised its findings, the Trial Chamber will now give its verdict. Mr. Kabashi, would you please stand. For the reasons summarised above, this Trial Chamber, having found you guilty on 31 August 2011, of the following charges: Count 1, contempt of the Tribunal by knowingly and wilfully interfering with the Tribunal's administration of justice on 5 June 2007, and; Count 2, contempt of the Tribunal by knowingly and wilfully interfering with the Tribunal's administration of justice on 20 November 2007. Hereby sentences you, Mr. Kabashi, to a single sentence of two months of imprisonment. You are entitled to credit for the period of time you have been in custody, which amounts to 31 days. Mr. Kabashi, you may be seated. This concludes the delivery of the sentencing judgement which will now be made publicly available. And before we adjourn, I would like to verify with Mr Karnavas whether he has been able to follow the pronouncement of sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have been able to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr Karnavas. The Trial Chamber stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.43 p.m.
